newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ROWELL AND CARLING READY TO STEP DOWN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ROWELL AND CARLING READY TO STEP DOWN.

text.p: England coach Jack Rowell and former captain Will Carling have both hinted that they will walk away from international rugby at the end of this season.

Rowell, who has steered England to Five Nations titles in each of the past two years, chose the day of his side's showdown with France at Twickenham to cast doubt on whether he will seek to renew his contract when it expires in June following England's tour to Argentina.
"We're in the professional era and increasingly the job takes a lot of time," said Rowell, who currently combines his England duties with a hectic business career.
"It's in the balance. We've been working hard so if I go it will be with reluctance," he told BBC radio Five Live on Saturday.
Carling, 31, told the Daily Mail newspaper he was treating the French match as possibly his last home game for England.

"There is a time to go and I have always wanted to get that timing right," said Carling, who will be winning his 71st cap. "I don't want to overstay my welcome. When the season is over I'm going to have a big think about my future."
Carling has already ruled himself out of this year's Lions tour to South Africa, so could make his farewell against Wales in Cardiff on March 15.
